health_review_content.scope: independent bounded review of restored-controller health helper
limits: This review does not establish that restoration has occurred or that the receipt, PID, status, or NAS paths currently exist.
The live watch_status is intentionally treated as mutable health state; immutable launch provenance comes from the rehashed attempt and restoration receipt.
The actual health helper must be invoked later with the concrete restoration_complete.json path and its exact SHA256.

findings: TaskValidateConfig runs before lease creation and preserves exact activation HEAD, runtime, source, publisher, settings, and cancelled-driver bindings.
The launcher requires original activation_complete evidence, exact owned STOP hash, zero TaskWatchers inventory, and a prepared action before its create-only lease claim.
The lease owner comes from the frozen STOP payload and its 3600-second duration exactly matches the frozen publisher lease_seconds ceiling.
Exactly one hidden private-Python process is started with publisher_quiescent48.py dispatch --request --lease from the repository working directory.

Native WaitForExit completes before Refresh and ExitCode capture. A publisher nonzero exit does not throw merely because of its exit code, so terminal evidence still records the actual native exit code, log hashes, action readback, and confirmed PID absence.
The launcher contains no Stop-Process, Remove-Item, retry loop, automatic restoration, NAS operation, queue implementation, or second publisher start.
Existing lease/start/terminal/log paths cause fail-closed refusal, preserving a prior attempt. Restoration handoff remains a separate root-reviewed action after result inspection.
limitations: The current transition config builder intentionally does not bind this later launcher; the actual milestone must separately bind the exact reviewed launcher SHA-256 before use.

A wrapper-level I/O or Start-Process exception can leave only the already-created lease and any logs/start evidence reached before the exception; there is deliberately no automatic retry, kill, or restoration. Root must inspect those artifacts and live process absence before constructing a terminal handoff.
This review does not claim that an actual publisher process was launched or completed.
publisher_launcher_review_content.conclusion: PASS for one-time root-controlled use after separately hash-binding these exact source bytes.

scope: One native publisher launch after reviewed quiescence; manually reviewed terminal handoff to original-settings restoration; future health PID is bound by the immutable restoration receipt.
limits: The publisher launcher is separately hash-bound because the transition builder binds its original six transition files only.
A wrapper-level start or I/O failure requires authentic reached evidence and manual inspection, never a fake publisher PID, automatic retry, or forced process termination.
